title: Observability: grafana-pg PG-ssl cert-rotate (standby-first, no restart)
description: cert-rotate on the observability tier now ALSO rotates the Grafana state-DB pair grafana-pg (GAP #5, v0.8.8)  --  previously a graceful skip. The shared PgSslCertRotator rotates the PG17 streaming pair STANDBY-FIRST then PRIMARY: it forces each node's nexus-vault-agent to re-issue the leaf (remove the rendered bundle.pem -> restart the agent -> re-render -> split to server.crt/server.key) then SIGHUP-reloads postgresql@17-main (NOT a restart), so PG re-reads the leaf for new connections while existing sessions + the streaming-replication connection keep running. Live-verified 2026-07-07.

prerequisites.smokeGate: grafana-pg pair on the current Vault root (vault-agents active); observability tier up for the full-tier verb

steps.command: ssh -i $NEXUS_SSH_KEY nexusadmin@192.168.70.180 'sudo openssl x509 -in /etc/nexus-grafana-pg/tls/server.crt -noout -serial | sed "s/serial=//"'; ssh -i $NEXUS_SSH_KEY nexusadmin@192.168.70.181 'sudo openssl x509 -in /etc/nexus-grafana-pg/tls/server.crt -noout -serial | sed "s/serial=//"'

observe.what: the CURRENT leaf serial on grafana-pg-1 (.180) and grafana-pg-2 (.181)  --  record them to compare after rotation

the per-node old/new serial table: grafana-pg-2 (standby) rotates BEFORE grafana-pg-1 (primary); both show a fresh newSerial (different from step 1). The primary is rotated LAST  --  a failed standby rotation would leave it untouched.
PG stays active  --  the rotation is a SIGHUP reload, not a restart (no dropped connections)

whatProves: grafana-pg TLS-leaf rotation is a real, in-CLI operation (not a DR-runbook deferral): the vault-agent re-issues the leaf and PG picks it up via a SIGHUP reload, standby-first, without a restart. The Grafana state DB gets fresh certs with no service interruption.
